title: BespokeCloudToolchainServices
description: Master-plan placement and requirements for Oyatie Cloud tenant-facing SCM, CI, and CD services. The control planes are bespoke Rust services; external OSS systems are bridge adapters or reference shapes, not permanent product substitutes.

_meta.source_request: Founder refinement: SCM, CI, and CD are cloud offerings to tenants; they must be bespoke Rust services that function well in Oyatie Cloud, while internal and tenant pipelines stay isolated, secure, and separate.

_meta.latest_refinement: Founder refinement applied: retired external SCM/CI/CD substrates are not interim authorities; GitHub/GitHub Actions are PR/publication/shadow adapters only, `oya` CLI is retired from CI authority, cloud-ci/oya-ci is Rust/Prow/Tide-shaped, Tide owns merge-queue admission now (Phase-0 placement, Phase-1 scale), and internal/tenant pipelines remain isolated.

masterplan_placement.relationship_to_existing_gitops_vcs: ADR-0363 remains binding for retiring the bespoke agentic-VCS CLI/wrapper. Current agent lanes use plain git plus the GitHub PR/publication adapter; durable authority moves to the Sapling-inspired Rust native SCM service/control plane. CI authority lives in the cloud-ci/oya-ci Prow-shaped service per ADR-0513: Tide owns merge admission, and `oya` CLI entrypoints are retirement/migration inputs only, not branch-protection producers.

product_posture.offering_type: Oyatie Cloud developer-platform services offered to internal Oyatie teams and external tenants
product_posture.bespoke_definition: The control plane, policy engine, admission engine, queue/reconciler state machine, tenant isolation model, APIs, billing/metering, audit chain, and user-visible UX are first-party Rust services. OSS tools may be used as bridge adapters, execution substrate, or reference shape, but cannot be the permanent product control plane.
product_posture.language_requirement: Rust for first-party control planes, CLIs, gate crates, reconcilers, webhooks, policy evaluators, state machines, and adapters; no new shell/python except explicit bootstrap/host-prelude allowlist with deletion criteria.
product_posture.cloud_fit: Runs as Oyatie Cloud services on the Talos/Kubernetes substrate with OpenBao/OpenTelemetry/Cedar/audit-chain integration, tenant quotas, metering, SLOs, DR, and regional/compliance-pack controls.

services.purpose: Tenant-facing source control and change graph service for monorepo and multi-repo tenants.
bridge_today: GitHub PRs, branch protection, commit statuses, webhooks as publication/status adapters
destination_capabilities: server-side change graph and stacked diffs
projected-state merge train with reverse-dependency indexing
tenant-scoped repository namespaces and policy-aware access graph
lazy materialization / virtual workspace only after measured scale trigger
directory-branch/subtree metadata support for branch-like flows without repo-wide merge graph explosion
services.cutover_rule: GitHub remains a collaboration/publication adapter until ADR-0510 numeric triggers or tenant-product demand justify the bespoke server. The Rust SCM API/admission/status layers are built now so the eventual storage/provider swap is an adapter cutover, not a contract rewrite.

services.purpose: Tenant-facing continuous-integration service with hermetic builds, bespoke gates, merge queues, and evidence emission.
bridge_today: Prow-shaped Rust cloud-ci/oya-ci controller path is the current CI direction and required-context producer.
GitHub PR/status publication remains an adapter; GitHub Actions remains compatibility/shadow evidence only, not durable CI authority.

Buck2 affected selection is the execution substrate during migration and after cutover; Cargo full mirrors are retired from active CI authority and may appear only as release-optimization or metadata-only evidence per specs/buck2-authority-policy.json.
destination_capabilities: required full bespoke gate context for protected branches
affected fast feedback plus full mirror for merge authority
trunk-sourced gate definitions with PR code as untrusted data
hermetic toolchain, CAS/RBE, deterministic test selection, structured failure summaries
merge queue / tide / batch / speculative projected-state validation
reviewer-agent and multispectrum evidence as first-class status requirements
services.enforcement_rule: The bespoke-CI required context is produced by the Prow-shaped cloud-ci control plane (oya-ci-controller) or its minimal Rust bridge adapter from trusted trunk/controller-sourced gate definitions, treating candidate PR bytes as untrusted data. Cloud-ci/oya-ci is the merge authority; Buck2 is the build/test execution substrate during migration and after cutover. Cargo is not CI/CD/build authority except for documented production release image/binary optimization evidence and Buck2 graph metadata exceptions. The `oya` CLI is retired from CI authority: `oya verify` and `oya gate` invocations may be inventoried as legacy local mirrors or migration inputs, but they cannot satisfy branch-protection merge or Phase-0 exit authority. Branch protection must require explicit oya-ci-required; RED if a plan-required context is missing, affected-only, buck2-affected-only, local-mirror-only, maps to any `oya` CLI invocation, or can be weakened by candidate PR bytes. Tide/merge queue belongs inside cloud-ci (`oya-ci-tide`) now: Phase 0 places and tests the admission contract; Phase 1 scales projected-state, batching, auto-rebase, and auto-regeneration.

services.purpose: Tenant-facing continuous-delivery and progressive-deployment service for applications, configuration, infrastructure, and policy changes.
bridge_today: No retired external CD controller is interim authority.
GitHub Actions CD is dry-run/artifact evidence only while the native release conveyor is built.
Existing desired-state/canary/workflow controller concepts are pattern references to reimplement behind Oyatie CD contracts, not active deployment authorities.
destination_capabilities: release ledger with immutable source/build/test/prod transitions
canary, blue-green, ring/cell rollout, automatic rollback and breakglass audit
configuration and infrastructure deployment pipelines, not only app code
drift detection plus desired-state reconciliation across tenant cells
per-tenant deployment policy, quota, compliance pack, region and data-residency enforcement
services.cutover_rule: The permanent user-facing product contract is oya-cd/release-conveyor. Historical desired-state, rollout, event, or workflow controller patterns may inform design, but they are not interim deployment authorities. Oya-cd parity must prove desired/live reconciliation, health, rollback, audit, canary analysis, and multi-cluster tenant isolation before any production CD claim.

tenant_isolation_contract.rule: Oyatie internal pipelines and every tenant pipeline are isolated, secure, and separate. Internal dogfood is tenant=oyatie-internal, not a privileged shared lane.
tenant_isolation_contract.control_plane: May be pooled only behind mandatory tenant-context authorization, per-tenant object ownership, and default-deny policy. Every API object carries tenant_id, region/cell, data_class, policy_domain, and audit_chain_ref.
tenant_isolation_contract.execution_plane: Default separate K8s namespace, service account, NetworkPolicy, runner pool quota, workspace volume, artifact namespace, log/evidence namespace, secret scope, and status callback identity per tenant. Regulated tiers may require dedicated cell/cluster/account equivalents.
tenant_isolation_contract.data_plane: Tenant repositories, object stores, CAS artifacts, SBOM/provenance, logs, traces, cache keys, deployment manifests, release ledgers, and audit events are partitioned by tenant. Cross-tenant cache reuse is denied by default except for explicitly public, content-addressed, policy-labeled artifacts with no tenant secrets or environment influence.
identity_and_secret_rules: Per-tenant OIDC/workload identity and OpenBao/KMS secret scopes.
Build jobs receive only scoped, time-bound credentials for their tenant and job.
Internal Oyatie jobs cannot assume tenant identities except through audited breakglass with TTL and reviewer approval.
network_rules: No runner pod can reach another tenant's workspace, cache namespace, artifact namespace, or webhook callback endpoint.
Egress is deny-by-default with tenant policy allowlists.
Service mesh / network policy labels include tenant_id and pipeline_id and are verified by admission gates.
audit_rules: Every SCM/CI/CD state transition emits audit-chain events with tenant_id, actor, workload identity, source revision, artifact digest, policy verdict, and rollback pointer.
Tenant administrators can view their own evidence and logs only; Oyatie operators see aggregate health unless breakglass is approved.
hard_separation_invariants: Separate tenant_id on every SCM repository, ChangeSet, CI run, artifact, cache entry, evidence record, release object, deploy target, secret lease, and audit event.

Separate execution identity per tenant pipeline: namespace, service account, workload identity, network policy, runner pool quota, workspace volume, artifact/log/evidence namespace, and status callback identity.
Internal Oyatie jobs run under tenant_id=oyatie-internal and cannot share credentials, caches, workspaces, release ledgers, or bypass gates with customer tenants.
Cross-tenant reads/writes are default-deny and test-fixtured; exceptions require explicit public content-addressed artifact policy or TTL breakglass with reviewer approval and audit-chain evidence.

sequence.name: Prow/cloud-ci enforcement baseline before Phase-0 execution
sequence.deliverable: Branch protection and live producers prove the current required context is produced by cloud-ci/oya-ci from trusted trunk/controller state; no `oya` CLI invocation is accepted as merge/exit authority, or Phase-0 execution remains blocked/honest-advisory only.

sequence.name: Bridge product contracts
sequence.deliverable: Publish cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd APIs, tenant isolation matrix, SLOs, quotas, audit schemas, and adapter boundaries while using GitHub/GitHub Actions only as PR/publication/shadow evidence adapters and not as durable CI/CD authority.

sequence.name: Rust control-plane MVPs
sequence.deliverable: oya-scm admission/status façade, oya-ci controller/tide required contexts, and oya-cd release-ledger/reconciler façade run for tenant=oyatie-internal and at least one sandbox tenant with hard isolation tests.

sequence.name: Tenant offering private preview
sequence.deliverable: External tenant sandbox can create repo/pipeline/release, run isolated CI, deploy to tenant cell via CD bridge, inspect evidence, and rollback without access to internal or other-tenant state.

sequence.name: Bridge-to-bespoke cutovers
sequence.deliverable: Cut over GitHub/GitHub Actions adapter/shadow surfaces only when native SCM, oya-ci, and release-conveyor parity, isolation, reliability, and scale triggers are green; otherwise keep adapter boundaries explicit and continue building Rust service contracts.

acceptance_criteria: Masterplan and sequencing sidecar reference this spec as the placement for SCM/CI/CD toolchain service work.
Branch-protection-context guard REDs when a required bespoke CI context is missing, affected-only, buck2-affected-only, local-mirror-only, or produced by any `oya` CLI invocation.

Tide/merge-queue placement is explicit in cloud-ci (`oya-ci-tide`): Phase 0 proves admission-contract fixtures; Phase 1 scales projected-state batching/auto-rebase without reopening the ownership decision.

Known-BAD fixture proves candidate PR code cannot weaken its own required status producer, gate definition, branch-protection mapping, or runner isolation; protected gate definitions are sourced from trusted trunk/controller state and treat PR bytes as untrusted data.
cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd each have Rust control-plane package plans and bridge adapter boundaries.
Internal pipeline and each tenant pipeline have separate tenant_id, namespace, runner identity, secrets, artifact namespace, logs/evidence, release ledger, and audit-chain partition.
Known-BAD fixtures prove tenant A cannot read/use tenant B repositories, artifacts, caches, logs, secrets, statuses, deployment manifests, or rollback handles.
Known-BAD fixtures prove tenant code cannot weaken its own gate, alter runner isolation, or bypass CD promotion policy.
CD progressive delivery uses SLI/SLO canary evaluation, staged exposure, automatic rollback, and breakglass audit before any production claim.
OSS bridges have deletion or parity criteria and cannot be referenced as permanent product substitutes in customer-facing claims.

T-ISOLATION-0: A fixture proving tenant A cannot read, write, cache-hit, status-update, deploy, or fetch logs/evidence/secrets for tenant B, and that tenant=oyatie-internal has no implicit bypass, is blocking before SCM/CI/CD are exposed as cloud services.

Any mechanically-enforced, production-ready, tenant-facing, isolated, or hyperscaler-grade claim about cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd must satisfy /specs/hyperscaler-production-readiness-claim-contract.json; otherwise the claim is labeled target/non-claim and blocked from authority surfaces by the claim-ceiling gate.
non_goals: Do not build a Piper/Mononoke-class storage server before ADR-0510 scale or tenant-product triggers justify it.
Do not expose retired external SCM/CI/CD substrates or GitHub/GitHub Actions as the permanent branded tenant product; expose Oyatie SCM/CI/CD APIs and UX.
Do not share execution workspaces, secrets, artifact namespaces, or mutable caches between tenants.
Do not weaken the current enforced bridge while building the bespoke destination.
Do not use `oya verify` or `oya gate` as required branch-protection producers; port semantics into Rust cloud-ci gate crates/adapters.
